definitions.gloss: to repent, to reform oneself, to mend one's ways
definitions.explanation: To deeply regret past wrongdoing and resolve to change one's behavior. Carries a moral and sometimes religious weight.

examples.japanese: {過去|かこ}の{過|あやま}ちを{悔|く}い{改|あらた}める。
{彼|かれ}は{自分|じぶん}の{行|おこな}いを{悔|く}い{改|あらた}め、{真面目|まじめ}に{生|い}きると{誓|ちか}った。
examples.english: He repented of his actions and vowed to live honestly.

examples.japanese: {罪|つみ}を{悔|く}い{改|あらた}めなければ、{許|ゆる}されることはない。
examples.english: Unless you repent of your sins, you will not be forgiven.

notes:
A compound verb from {悔|く}いる (to regret) + {改|あらた}める (to reform). The combination emphasizes not just feeling regret but actively changing one's conduct. Common in religious, moral, and literary contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {罪|つみ}を{悔|く}い{改|あらた}める: to repent of one's sins
- {過|あやま}ちを{悔|く}い{改|あらた}める: to repent of one's mistakes
- {行|おこな}いを{悔|く}い{改|あらた}める: to reform one's behavior

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {後悔|こうかい}する: to regret — focuses on the feeling of regret without implying reform
- {反省|はんせい}する: to reflect on one's actions — more everyday; implies self-examination
- {改心|かいしん}する: to have a change of heart — focuses on the inner transformation
